subject: chemistry
title: Acyl chlorides and acylation
key_idea: Acyl chlorides are very reactive derivatives of carboxylic acids. They are made with SOCl₂, PCl₅ or PCl₃. Water, alcohols, ammonia and amines attack the carbonyl carbon by nucleophilic addition–elimination, replacing the chlorine.

sections.heading: Acyl chlorides and how they are made

blocks.text: An acyl chloride has a chlorine atom in place of the –OH of a carboxylic acid. This section covers the structures and how to make them.

items.meaning: R–COCl. The carbonyl carbon is joined to Cl, for example ethanoyl chloride, CH₃COCl.
(RCO)₂O. Two acyl groups joined through one oxygen, for example ethanoic anhydride.
R–CONH₂, or with an alkyl group on the nitrogen, R–CONHR'. The carbonyl carbon is joined to N.
R–COOR'. The carbonyl carbon is joined to an –OR' group.

items: Thionyl chloride is convenient because both by-products are gases, which leave the mixture.
The acyl chloride is separated from the other products by distillation (for PCl₅ and PCl₃).
Acyl chlorides react with water, so the reaction mixture must be kept dry.
Acyl chlorides are made from carboxylic acids with SOCl₂, PCl₅ or PCl₃.
SOCl₂ gives only gaseous by-products.
Amides contain C–N, esters contain C–O.

blocks.text: Acyl chlorides react with nucleophiles that contain an –OH or –NH group. Pick a reagent to see what ethanoyl chloride gives.

diagram.alt: A predictor. Pick a nucleophile to see what it forms with ethanoyl chloride at room temperature.
diagram.prompt: Pick a nucleophile to react with ethanoyl chloride.

options.label: Water
results: Vigorous reaction, steamy fumes of HCl

options.label: Ethanol
results: Vigorous reaction, steamy fumes, fruity smell

options.label: Phenol
options.explanation: CH₃COCl + C₆H₅OH → CH₃COOC₆H₅ + HCl. Phenol is not readily esterified by a carboxylic acid.

options.label: Concentrated ammonia
results: HCl, which forms NH₄Cl with excess NH₃
Vigorous reaction, white smoke of NH₄Cl
options.explanation: CH₃COCl + NH₃ → CH₃CONH₂ + HCl, then NH₃ + HCl → NH₄Cl

options.label: A primary amine, CH₃NH₂
results: HCl, which forms a salt with excess amine

items: All the reactions occur at room temperature.
Acyl chlorides esterify phenol. A carboxylic acid does not react readily with phenol.
Acyl chlorides give a better yield of ester than a carboxylic acid, because the reaction is not reversible.
Acylation means adding an acyl group, R–CO, to a molecule.
Acyl chloride + water, alcohol, phenol, ammonia or amine: the Cl is replaced.
HCl is always the other product.
Reactions are fast at room temperature.

blocks.text: The carbonyl carbon is δ+ because it is bonded to both oxygen and chlorine. A nucleophile attacks it in two stages: addition, then elimination.

items.text: The nucleophile (H₂O, ROH, NH₃ or RNH₂) uses its lone pair to attack the δ+ carbon. The C=O π bond breaks and the electrons move onto oxygen. This gives an intermediate with O⁻ and a positive charge on the nucleophile atom.
The lone pair on O⁻ reforms the C=O double bond. The C–Cl bond breaks and Cl⁻ leaves.
The positively charged atom loses an H⁺. This combines with Cl⁻ to make HCl.

items: The reaction is called nucleophilic **addition–elimination**.
Addition: the nucleophile adds to the carbonyl carbon.
Elimination: chloride is lost, and the carbonyl group is reformed.
The mechanism is the same for water, alcohols, ammonia and amines. Only the nucleophile changes.
Nucleophile attacks the δ+ carbon, then Cl⁻ is eliminated.
The tetrahedral intermediate has an O⁻ and the nucleophile attached.
HCl forms as the second product.

checks.q: Write an equation for the reaction of propanoyl chloride with ethanol, and name the organic product.
checks.a: CH₃CH₂COCl + CH₃CH₂OH → CH₃CH₂COOCH₂CH₃ + HCl. The product is ethyl propanoate.

checks.q: Outline the mechanism for the reaction of ethanoyl chloride with ammonia.
checks.a: The lone pair on nitrogen attacks the δ+ carbon of C=O. The C=O π bond breaks, giving an intermediate with O⁻ and N⁺. The lone pair on O⁻ reforms C=O and Cl⁻ is lost. H⁺ is lost from nitrogen, giving ethanamide and HCl.

checks.q: Suggest why thionyl chloride is a convenient reagent for making acyl chlorides.
checks.a: The other products, SO₂ and HCl, are both gases, so they leave the reaction mixture and the acyl chloride is easy to obtain.

blocks.text: This part covers the products this course names for acyl chlorides.

items: Acyl chlorides are used in synthesis to make esters, carboxylic acids, and primary and secondary amides.
Primary amide: from ammonia, RCONH₂. Secondary amide: from a primary amine, RCONHR'.
Phenol is esterified by an acyl chloride because it is not readily esterified by a carboxylic acid.

blocks.text: This part covers the four reactions in the specification.

items: Identify the acyl chloride group, –COCl, and the ester group, –COO–.
Water gives a carboxylic acid, an alcohol gives an ester, concentrated ammonia gives an amide, and an amine gives an N-substituted amide.
Use concentrated ammonia and excess amine, so that the HCl formed is neutralised.

blocks.text: This part covers acid anhydrides, aspirin and the preparation of a pure organic solid and liquid.

items: Acid anhydrides react with water, alcohols, ammonia and primary amines like acyl chlorides. The second product is a carboxylic acid, not HCl.
Aspirin is made from 2-hydroxybenzoic acid. Ethanoic anhydride is preferred industrially to ethanoyl chloride.
Ethanoic anhydride is **cheaper**.
It is **less corrosive** and reacts **less vigorously** with water.
It does not produce HCl, which is corrosive and toxic.

blocks.text: Preparing a pure organic solid and a pure organic liquid

items.text: Warm the reagents, then cool to crystallise the crude product.
Filter under reduced pressure, then recrystallise from a minimum of hot solvent and dry.
Measure the melting point. A pure solid melts sharply at the data-book value. An impure solid melts lower and over a range.
Use a separating funnel to wash and separate the organic layer. Dry it with an anhydrous salt, then distil and collect the fraction at the known boiling point.

blocks.text: This part covers named examples and why acyl chlorides hydrolyse more easily than other chlorides.

items: Esters from acyl chlorides: ethyl ethanoate from ethanoyl chloride and ethanol, and phenyl benzoate from benzoyl chloride and phenol.
Making acyl chlorides: PCl₃ with heat, PCl₅, or SOCl₂.
Amides form with ammonia, and with primary or secondary amines, at room temperature.

rows: The carbonyl carbon is attached to two electronegative atoms, O and Cl. It is very δ+ and accepts a nucleophile easily.
Slow, needs warming with aqueous alkali
The carbon is only attached to one electronegative atom, so it is less δ+.
A lone pair on Cl overlaps with the ring π system. The C–Cl bond is stronger and has some double-bond character. The ring electrons repel the nucleophile.

blocks.text: Order of ease of hydrolysis: acyl chloride > alkyl chloride > aryl chloride.
